subject: Post-call: Model evaluations & multilingual quality checks \u0014 next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Ana Silva <ana.silva@globexretail.com>; Tom Becker <t.becker@globexretail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Model evaluations & multilingual quality checks  next steps

Hi Ana / Tom,

Thanks again for the call earlier  really helpful to hear more about Globex's roadmap for localized customer support (FR/DE/ES) and plans in APAC (JA/KO). A quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned: 

- Goal: improve automated support responses across EU + APAC locales while keeping latency under 300ms p50 for user-facing flows.
- Key constraints: on-device PII redaction, EU data residency for EU customers, and tight cost targets for peak shopping events.

Recommended immediate next steps:
1) Well run a model evaluation using your sample prompt set across target locales (FR, DE, ES, JA, KO).
2) SE team (Neha) will build per-locale prompt templates + evaluation harness and share benchmark links.
3) Schedule a 60-min follow-up to review quantitative/regression analysis and pick a candidate model for a 2-week POC.

Ive attached our high-level model recommendation sheet and the prompt set you shared during the call  Neha and I will seed the evaluation job and share links by Monday.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>
To: Ana Silva <ana.silva@globexretail.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model evaluations & multilingual quality checks  initial benchmarks and next steps

Hi Ana / Marissa,

Thanks  I kicked off the evaluation jobs this morning. High-level notes from the first pass (summary + links below):

What I ran:
- Candidate models: redwood-ml-2.7b, redwood-ml-7b-qat, open-llm-multilingual-v1
- Locales: fr-FR, de-DE, es-ES, ja-JP, ko-KR
- Metrics: response quality (top-1 human eval proxy), BLEU/chrF for translation-transfer cases, latency p50/p95, token cost estimate.

Preliminary results (very early):
- redwood-ml-7b-qat shows consistently better quality in FR/DE/ES for customer-support style prompts with a ~12% lift in top-1 quality vs open-llm-multilingual-v1.
- open-llm-multilingual-v1 is significantly cheaper but shows regression in JA/KO on brand-voice and politeness (higher hallucination rate on domain terms).
- redwood-ml-2.7b is fastest (p50 ~ 180ms) but has a larger quality gap in non-Latin scripts.

Links: 
- Evaluation dashboard (per-locale): https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/globex/mt-eu-v1
- Prompt set & per-case annotations: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cModelEvals

Attachments included in the Drive: multilingual_prompt_set_v1.csv (prompt templates + expected outputs), per-locale example failures.csv.

Open items / asks:
1) Ana  can you confirm if we should prioritize brand-voice/low-hallucination for JA/KO over raw BLEU? That will change model selection.
2) Marissa  Rishi asked whether we can propose an interim config for EU residency of logs during evals (we can spin dedicated ephemeral storage in FRA).

Next steps: Ill prep a 1-slide summary per locale and share it ahead of the Wed 29 meeting. If everyone is OK, Ill also spin up a canary POC with redwood-ml-7b-qat + aggressive prefix caching for EU traffic.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.inference
[Attachment: per-locale_example_failures.csv (CSV, 18KB)]
